event-hype_wave-trader: Hype buyers are starting to rush into ZOOMZ. Many are buying just because others are buying. Its price may climb fast for about half a minute. Then early buyers may take profit, and the price may fade. Hype can push a price up fast, and it usually fades just as fast.
event-hype_wave-builder: ZOOMZ launched on a bonding curve, so each purchase pushes its price up automatically. Hype buyers are rushing in, and the climb may run for about half a minute. Early buyers may then take profit, and the price may fade. A price rising from buying alone is not the same as value being built.
event-halving-explorer: VAULT just had a halving. Now it makes half as many new coins. That means fewer new coins to sell. Nothing jumps right away. Nobody loses coins they hold. Fewer new coins can make each coin rarer over time.
event-halving-trader: VAULT's halving just started. New coin creation is cut in half. The hard cap of 21,000,000 is unchanged, but supply now grows more slowly. Miners have fewer new coins to sell, so selling pressure may ease slowly. Watch for a gradual change, not a jump. Coins you hold stay the same.
event-halving-builder: The reward for making new VAULT coins just halved. New issuance shrinks, but the 21,000,000 cap and every existing balance are unchanged. Because the date was public, traders may have priced it in already. Watch for a slow change in selling pressure, not an instant jump.
event-unlock-trader: A quarter of ORBIT's locked team and investor coins just unlocked. Some insiders sold at once, so the drop is already on the chart. ORBIT may recover part of the way. Then watch for more coins vesting little by little, which may press the price down slowly. More coins in circulation means more supply that can be sold.
event-unlock-builder: ORBIT's team and investors held locked coins. A quarter of that pile just unlocked at once, and some insiders sold, so the drop is already on the chart. The rest vests gradually. Watch for a partial bounce, then steady pressure as each release arrives. Checking an unlock schedule is part of reading a launch.
event-whale_dump-explorer: One whale just sold a huge pile of VAULT. A whale is one holder with lots of coins. The price dropped fast. VAULT itself did not change. The price may come back part of the way. Selling everything in a scare can make a loss real.
event-whale_dump-trader: One whale just sold a huge pile of VAULT in one go, so the drop is already on the chart. A big trade moves the pool price a lot. Nothing about VAULT changed. The price may recover part of the way. Panic sellers who dump everything lock in the loss. One big holder is concentration risk.
event-whale_dump-builder: A whale just sold a large VAULT position into the pool in one trade. Under x times y equals k, a big sale moves the price far, so the drop is already on the chart. VAULT's design did not change. The price may recover part of the way. Selling everything right after the drop can lock in the loss.
event-rug_pull-builder: BLOOP's NPC creator is pulling almost all the L$ out of its pool and selling their bag. When the market restarts, the price falls almost to zero. Holders cannot sell for anything close to what they paid. The red flags were visible: the creator held 60% of the coins, the pool was not locked, and hype pumped the price first.
event-depeg_scare-explorer: Scared holders sold PEG. It is at about L$0.96 now. PEG aims to stay at L$1.00. Watch what happens next. Traders who can swap PEG for L$1 may buy the cheap coins. That may bring PEG back to L$1.00 soon.
event-depeg_scare-trader: PEG is a stablecoin that aims for L$1.00, backed 1:1. Scared holders just sold, and it sits at about L$0.96. Traders who can swap PEG back for L$1 may buy the cheap coins. Watch PEG drift back toward L$1.00 within about 15 seconds. Stablecoins can depeg, and backing is what pulls them back.
event-depeg_scare-builder: Fear selling pushed PEG to about L$0.96, below its L$1.00 target. A peg holds through arbitrage: anyone who can swap PEG for L$1 profits by buying it cheap. That buying may close the gap within about 15 seconds. A peg is only as strong as its backing and its swap route.
event-wash_volume-builder: Look at the real and wash volume overlay. An NPC bot is trading FUEL with itself all session. Wash trading means one trader buys from and sells to itself. The volume bars look busy, but the price barely moves because no real buyer is behind that volume. Watch real volume and price, not just bar height.
event-copycat-builder: An NPC just listed a look-alike of your coin with Official in its name, at the same price, and it is hyping it. Look-alikes borrow trust they have not earned. Your coin is the original and stays honest. Watch whether the copycat's pool stays in place. A name does not prove a coin is real.
event-copycat_rug-builder: The copycat's creator just pulled its pool. People who bought the copycat cannot sell it for anything close to what they paid. Your own coin keeps trading. Watch for the lesson: a matching price and a trusted-sounding name do not make a coin real.
gate-explorer-two-wants: You have L$50. A toy costs L$30 and a game costs L$40. You can't buy both. How do you choose well?
gate-explorer-save-wait: A bike costs L$40. You save L$10 every week and spend none of it. When can you buy the bike?
gate-explorer-scarce-stickers: A club makes only 100 special stickers. Then it prints 1,000,000 more just like them. What usually happens to each sticker's worth?
gate-trader-spread-risk: You have L$1,000. One of your coins might suddenly crash to nearly zero. Which setup would hurt the least?
gate-trader-more-buyers: A coin's price is steady. Twice as many people suddenly want to buy it, but the number for sale stays the same. What happens?
gate-trader-hype-reason: Which reason for buying a coin is hype?
gate-builder-unlock-effect: A coin will unlock a quarter of its locked team coins tomorrow, with the rest vesting slowly. What is the main thing to think about?
gate-builder-rug-flags: A new coin's creator holds 60% of its coins, and its pool is not locked. What does this combination mean?
gate-builder-fake-volume: A coin's trading volume spikes, but its price barely moves. The same trader appears on both sides of many trades. What is likely going on?
lesson-explorer-1: Think of stickers. A plain sticker is easy to find. A shiny gold one is rare. Kids will swap many plain stickers for one gold one. Rare things are worth more swaps.
lesson-explorer-2: Say a pot holds L$120 of value. All the coins share it equally. Slide to make more coins. Watch what each coin is worth.
lesson-explorer-3: VAULT can never go past 21,000,000 coins. No more can ever be made. That keeps it rare. Tap to compare keeping the cap with making lots more.
lesson-explorer-4: Rare is only half the story. A rare thing nobody wants is not worth much. People must want it too. Rare and wanted together make a higher price.
lesson-trader-1: Imagine your L$1,000 sits in one coin. If that coin drops, your whole pile drops with it. This is called concentration risk. One coin carries all the weight.
lesson-trader-2: Spreading means keeping money in several places, including L$ or PEG. Slide to put more into one coin. See how much is left for everything else.
lesson-trader-3: Hype is buying because everyone else is buying. A coin like ZOOMZ can climb fast this way. But the crowd moves on. Tap to see both halves of the cycle.
lesson-trader-4: A busy crowd tells you people are excited. It does not tell you the coin is sound. Ask what the coin does and who holds it. Then decide how much to risk.
lesson-builder-1: Every launch has the same parts. Creators make the coins, keep a share, and open a pool with some L$. Then they promote it. Four quick checks show whether a launch could hide a rug pull.
lesson-builder-2: BLOOP's creator holds 60% of its coins. Slide the creator's share. Here we pretend all the coins together are worth L$1,000. See what the creator could dump at once.
lesson-builder-3: The pool holds the L$ and coins that people trade against. A rug pull means creators pull that money out and sell their coins. Only an unlocked pool allows it. Tap to compare.
lesson-builder-4: A coin with Official in its name, loud hype and an unlocked pool is a pattern. Names cost nothing to copy. Check holders and the pool lock, not the label.
event-hype_wave-trader-question: ZOOMZ is climbing and everyone is buying. Which reaction fits a calm player in the lab?
event-hype_wave-builder-question: On a bonding curve, why does the ZOOMZ price rise as hype buyers pile in?
event-halving-explorer-question: You hold 10 VAULT when the halving happens. How many do you hold right after?
event-halving-trader-question: What is the most likely effect of the halving on VAULT's selling pressure?
event-halving-builder-question: The halving date was known long ago. Why might the price not jump the moment it happens?
event-unlock-trader-question: Why can an unlock push a price down when the project itself did not change?
event-unlock-builder-question: ORBIT has 1,000,000 locked coins. A quarter unlocks at once. How many join circulating supply now?
event-whale_dump-explorer-question: The VAULT price fell after a whale sold. VAULT itself did not change. What does a calm player do?
event-whale_dump-trader-question: VAULT dropped after a whale sold, and nothing about VAULT changed. Why can selling everything now hurt?
event-whale_dump-builder-question: Why does one big sale move the pool price more than many small sales?
event-rug_pull-builder-question: Which pair of facts was a red flag on BLOOP before the pool was pulled?
event-depeg_scare-explorer-question: PEG is at about L$0.96. Why may traders want to buy it?
event-depeg_scare-trader-question: PEG sits at about L$0.96, and traders can swap each PEG for L$1. What may their buying do?
event-depeg_scare-builder-question: What mechanism pulls PEG back toward L$1.00?
event-wash_volume-builder-question: FUEL's volume bars are tall, but its price barely moves. What is the best explanation?
event-copycat-builder-question: A coin with Official in its name copies yours and is loudly hyped. What is the best check?
event-copycat_rug-builder-question: Why can copycat buyers not sell near what they paid?
lesson-explorer-quiz: VAULT can never go past 21,000,000 coins. What would happen if someone could suddenly make millions more?
lesson-trader-quiz: A player puts L$900 of L$1,000 into ZOOMZ because everyone is buying it. What is the main risk?
lesson-builder-quiz: Which launch has the most rug pull warning signs?
event-hype_wave-trader-question-explain: Hype is buying because others buy. A calm player checks the reason and limits risk, because hype usually fades about as fast as it rises.
event-hype_wave-builder-question-explain: A bonding curve sets price by how much has been bought. More buying moves it up, whether or not anything about the coin improved.
event-halving-explorer-question-explain: A halving only slows down new coins being made. The coins you already hold stay yours, so you still have 10.
event-halving-trader-question-explain: A halving slows new supply. Miners have less to sell, so the effect builds slowly. It never takes coins away from holders.
event-halving-builder-question-explain: When an event is scheduled and public, buyers and sellers often act early. Also, a halving only slows new supply, so its effect builds gradually.
event-unlock-trader-question-explain: An unlock adds to circulating supply. When insiders sell some of it, extra supply meets the same demand, and the price can fall.
event-unlock-builder-question-explain: A quarter of 1,000,000 is 250,000. The other 750,000 stay locked and vest little by little, so more supply may arrive later.
event-whale_dump-explorer-question-expla: The coin did not change, only one big seller moved the price. A calm look first helps you avoid turning a drop into a real loss.
event-whale_dump-trader-question-explain: The drop came from one large trade, not from a problem with VAULT. Selling everything in a panic turns a dip into a real loss, and the price may still recover part of the way.
event-whale_dump-builder-question-explai: Price is L$ in the pool divided by coins in the pool. A large sale changes that balance a lot in one step, which is price impact.
event-rug_pull-builder-question-explain: A creator with most of the coins and an unlocked pool can drain the pool at any time. Every coin's pool follows the same price rule, so that is no warning sign.
event-depeg_scare-explorer-question-expl: If one PEG can be swapped for L$1, buying it at about L$0.96 is a bargain. That buying pushes the price back up.
event-depeg_scare-trader-question-explai: Buying cheap PEG that can be swapped for L$1 adds demand. That demand lifts the price until the gap closes.
event-depeg_scare-builder-question-expla: The gap between about L$0.96 and L$1.00 is a profit for traders who can swap. Their buying lifts the price and closes the gap.
event-wash_volume-builder-question-expla: Real demand moves price. Tall bars with a flat price suggest wash trading: one trader on both sides, adding volume but no new buyers.
event-copycat-builder-question-explain: Anyone can type Official in a name or copy a price. The creator and the pool lock show whether the money can be pulled out.
event-copycat_rug-builder-question-expla: Prices come from the L$ and coins in a pool. With the L$ pulled out, nothing is left to pay sellers, so the price collapses.
gate-explorer-two-wants-explain: Money is limited, so every choice means giving something up. Thinking about which want matters most to you, and for how long, helps you choose well.
gate-explorer-save-wait-explain: L$10 each week adds up: L$10, L$20, L$30, then L$40 after four weeks. Waiting and saving a little at a time lets you afford bigger things.
gate-explorer-scarce-stickers-explain: When something is rare, people value it more. Make lots more, and each one is worth less. That is why VAULT has a hard cap on how many can ever exist.
gate-trader-spread-risk-explain: If one coin crashes, you only lose what you put in it. Here the most you could lose is L$300. Putting too much in one place is called concentration risk.
gate-trader-more-buyers-explain: When more people want something and the supply for sale stays the same, buyers compete. That pushes the price up. This is supply and demand.
gate-trader-hype-reason-explain: Hype means buying because everyone else is buying. A rush like that can lift a price fast, and it usually fades just as fast. Having your own reasons keeps you steady.
gate-builder-unlock-effect-explain: An unlock raises the circulating supply. If some insiders sell, that extra selling can push the price down. Vesting spreads the release out so it hits the market more gently.
gate-builder-rug-flags-explain: A huge creator share and an unlocked pool are both red flags. The creator could remove the money from the pool and sell, leaving holders unable to sell for anything near what they paid.
gate-builder-fake-volume-explain: Wash trading is one trader buying from and selling to itself. Volume looks busy, but there is no real demand, so the price barely moves. Busy volume alone does not prove interest.
lesson-explorer-quiz-explain: When more coins exist and the same people want them, each coin is easier to get. That makes each one worth less. The cap keeps VAULT rare.
lesson-trader-quiz-explain: Putting most money in one coin is concentration risk, and hype tends to fade. Spreading money across several places, including L$ or PEG, softens a fall.
lesson-builder-quiz-explain: A huge creator share plus an unlocked pool lets creators drain the money and sell, while hype brings in buyers. The other launches limit what creators can do.
path-explorer-u1-l1-1: Money has four jobs. You can earn it. You can save it. You can spend it. You can share it. Most days, you use more than one.
path-explorer-u1-l1-2: A need is something you must have to be safe and healthy. A want is something fun that you could live without. Both are okay. Needs come first.
path-explorer-u1-l1-3: Every time you get money, you choose. You can spend it today. You can keep some for later. Try both choices and see what changes.
path-explorer-u1-l1-4: In the lab, you start with L$1,000. Every L$ you spend leaves your pile. Slide to see how much is left after you spend.
path-explorer-u1-l1-quiz: You have L$100. Lunch this week costs L$30. A toy costs L$80. Which one is the need?
path-explorer-u1-l1-quiz-explain: Lunch is food, and food is a need. The toy is a want. You can enjoy it, but you can live without it.
path-explorer-u1-l2-1: Waiting can feel slow. But it gives you time. You can gather more money. You can also check if you still want the thing.
path-explorer-u1-l2-2: Say you see a game you like. You can buy it right away. Or you can wait a week. See what each choice gives you.
path-explorer-u1-l2-3: Say you want a L$120 game. You can save it in small steps. Slide the weeks. More weeks means a smaller step each week.
path-explorer-u1-l2-4: A plan has three steps. Say what you want. Check how much money you have. Decide how long you will wait. Use this plan in the lab too.
path-explorer-u1-l2-quiz: You save L$20 each week for a L$80 game. How many weeks until you can buy it?
path-explorer-u1-l2-quiz-explain: After each week you have L$20, then L$40, then L$60, then L$80. That is 4 weeks.
path-explorer-u1-c-q1: Which one is an example of earning money?
path-explorer-u1-c-q1-explain: Earning means getting money for work or help. Giving a gift is sharing, and keeping money in a jar is saving.
path-explorer-u1-c-q2: You start the lab with L$1,000. You keep L$700 and do not spend it. What is that called?
path-explorer-u1-c-q2-explain: Money you keep for later is savings. You did not spend it, and you did not give it away.
path-explorer-u1-c-q3: Which one is a want, not a need?
path-explorer-u1-c-q3-explain: Water and medicine keep you healthy, so they are needs. A third pair of fancy sneakers is fun, but you can live without it.
path-explorer-u1-c-q4: Why can waiting before you buy something help?
path-explorer-u1-c-q4-explain: Waiting gives you time to think, compare and save. It does not change prices, and saved money does not grow by magic.
path-explorer-u1-c-q5: You have L$50 and want a L$90 toy. You save L$10 each week. How many weeks do you wait?
path-explorer-u1-c-q5-explain: You need L$40 more, because L$90 minus L$50 is L$40. Saving L$10 each week, that takes 4 weeks.
path-trader-u1-l1-1: A budget is a plan for your money. You start the lab with L$1,000. A plan says how much to spend, how much to save, and how much to keep ready.
path-trader-u1-l1-2: Every L$ you put into coins is a L$ you cannot use elsewhere. Drag to set how much goes into coins. The rest of your L$1,000 stays free.
path-trader-u1-l1-3: Opportunity cost is the best thing you give up when you choose. Money is limited, so every choice skips another one. It is not a fee. It is the road not taken.
path-trader-u1-l1-4: Every choice gives something and skips something. Switch between the two choices to see what each one gives and what it gives up.
path-trader-u1-l1-quiz: Your budget is L$1,000. You keep L$150 in PEG and put L$500 into VAULT. How much is left for other choices?
path-trader-u1-l1-quiz-explain: Add what you have set aside: L$150 plus L$500 is L$650. Take that from L$1,000 and L$350 is left.
path-trader-u1-l2-1: Interest is a payment for letting someone use your money. Simple interest is paid only on your starting amount. So it stays the same size each year.
path-trader-u1-l2-2: Here L$1,000 earns 5 percent simple interest. That is L$50 every year. Drag to choose how many years you wait and watch the total grow.
path-trader-u1-l2-3: Compound interest is paid on your starting amount plus the interest you already earned. Each year the pile is bigger, so the next payment is bigger too. Compare both with 10 percent on L$1,000.
path-trader-u1-l2-4: Inflation means prices rise over time. If a snack costs L$10 now and L$11 next year, the same L$10 buys less. Money that sits still slowly loses buying power.
path-trader-u1-l2-quiz: You earn 5 percent simple interest on L$2,000 for 2 years. How much interest do you earn in total?
path-trader-u1-l2-quiz-explain: Simple interest is counted on the starting L$2,000 only. That is L$100 each year, so L$200 over two years.
path-trader-u1-c-q1: You start with L$1,000 and plan to keep L$250 as cash. How much can go into coins?
path-trader-u1-c-q1-explain: A budget splits your money. Take the L$250 you keep from L$1,000 and L$750 is left for coins.
path-trader-u1-c-q2: You can hold L$100 in PEG or put it into FUEL. You pick FUEL. What is the opportunity cost?
path-trader-u1-c-q2-explain: Opportunity cost is the best choice you gave up. Here that is the other use of the L$100, not the coin you picked.
path-trader-u1-c-q3: L$1,000 earns 10 percent compound interest. Year 1 pays L$100. What does year 2 pay?
path-trader-u1-c-q3-explain: In year 2 you earn interest on L$1,100, which includes the first interest. 10 percent of L$1,100 is L$110.
path-trader-u1-c-q4: A snack costs L$20 today and L$22 next year. What does this show?
path-trader-u1-c-q4-explain: Prices rising over time is inflation. Next year, the same L$20 buys less than it buys today.
path-trader-u1-c-q5: Your savings earn 2 percent a year, but prices rise 4 percent a year. What is true?
path-trader-u1-c-q5-explain: Prices grow faster than your interest. So even though your L$ total grows, it buys a little less each year.
path-builder-u1-l1-1: Compound growth means you earn on your earlier earnings too. Say L$1,000 grows 10% each year. Year one adds L$100. Year two adds L$110, because your base is now L$1,100.
path-builder-u1-l1-2: Compounding is slow at first, then it speeds up. Each year the base is bigger, so each year adds more. Over long periods, the number of years matters a lot.
path-builder-u1-l1-3: Inflation means prices tend to rise over time. If a snack costs L$10 now, it may cost more later. Money that just sits still can buy less each year.
path-builder-u1-l1-4: Real return is what you earn after inflation. Say your savings earn 5% a year. Inflation takes a bite out of that. Slide inflation up and watch your real return shrink toward zero. If inflation went higher than 5%, it would turn negative.
path-builder-u1-l1-quiz: Your L$1,000 earns 4% a year while prices rise 6% a year. What happens to what it can buy?
path-builder-u1-l1-quiz-explain: Real return is about 4% minus 6%, so roughly minus 2%. Your L$ number grows, but each L$ buys a little less.
path-builder-u1-l2-1: Higher possible return comes with bigger possible swings. PEG aims for L$1.00 and moves little. ZOOMZ can leap, and it can drop just as far. A chance of more comes with a chance of less.
path-builder-u1-l2-2: Speculation means betting on a price move that nobody can be sure of. It can pay, and it can cost. Compare two styles of coin and notice the trade.
path-builder-u1-l2-3: An emergency fund is money set aside for surprises, like a broken bike. It should be steady and easy to reach. In the lab, that means L$ or PEG. Coins that swing could be down on the day you need cash.
path-builder-u1-l2-4: The Money Health Score asks you to keep at least 10% of your money in L$ or PEG, and no coin above half. Slide to see what a steady share means out of L$1,000.
path-builder-u1-l2-quiz: A friend puts all L$1,000 into one meme coin because it might double. What do risk and return say?
path-builder-u1-l2-quiz-explain: Chances of more and chances of less travel together. Putting everything in one coin also leaves nothing steady for surprises.
path-builder-u1-c-q1: L$1,000 grows 10% a year. After year one you hold L$1,100. How much does year two add?
path-builder-u1-c-q1-explain: Year two earns 10% of L$1,100, which is L$110. Earning on your earlier earnings is what makes growth compound.
path-builder-u1-c-q2: Your savings earn 3% a year while prices rise 5% a year. What is your real return, roughly?
path-builder-u1-c-q2-explain: Real return is what you earn minus inflation. Three minus five is about minus two, so your money buys a little less.
path-builder-u1-c-q3: Which lab coin is built to move little, with a smaller chance of big gains?
path-builder-u1-c-q3-explain: PEG aims to stay at L$1.00, so it swings little. Hype coins like ZOOMZ can move far in both directions.
path-builder-u1-c-q4: You hold L$1,000. Which setup best keeps an emergency cushion?
path-builder-u1-c-q4-explain: Steady money in L$ or PEG covers surprises without selling coins on a bad day. Spreading the rest also limits one coin's damage.
path-builder-u1-c-q5: Two players earn the same yearly growth. Mia invests L$500 now. Leo invests L$500 ten years later. Who ends ahead?
path-builder-u1-c-q5-explain: Growth on growth needs time. Mia's L$500 gets ten extra rounds of earning on earlier earnings, so she usually ends ahead.
mc-k-compound: You save 100 baht. Each year the bank adds 10 baht for every 100 baht you have. You leave it all there for 2 years. How much do you have?
mc-k-inflation: Your money sits in a jar and earns nothing. Shop prices go up by 5 baht for every 100 baht each year. A year later, what can your money buy?
mc-k-spread: Which is usually safer for your savings?
mc-k-time: Someone will give you 100 baht. They can give it today or next year. Which is worth more to you?
mc-k-scam: A message says: “Send 500 baht today and get 5,000 baht next week. Only 10 places left!” What is this most likely?
mc-b-save: When you get money, how often do you keep some of it to save?
mc-b-plan: Before you buy something, how often do you check that you can really afford it?
mc-b-compare: How often do you compare prices before you buy?
mc-b-track: How often do you keep track of the money you spend?
mc-t-now: Which would you pick: 100 baht today, or 105 baht in one month?
mc-t-far: And this one: 100 baht in 6 months, or 105 baht in 7 months?
mc-r-flip: Pick one: 50 baht for sure, or flip a coin. Heads you get 120 baht, tails you get nothing.
mc-r-safe: Now pick again: 80 baht for sure, or flip a coin. Heads you get 120 baht, tails you get nothing.
mc-s-worship: Do you agree? “More money would fix all my problems.”
mc-s-status: Do you agree? “Expensive things show that a person is important.”
